dispatches.label: 16 Nov 2026
dispatches.author: steward
dispatches.title: SchneiTec Jupiter lists a record US$99 million green bond in Cambodia
dispatches.summary: On 16 November 2026 SchneiTec Jupiter listed a US$99 million green infrastructure project bond on the Cambodia Securities Exchange, a record for the exchange, anchoring a US$150 million package for a 350 MW solar plant in Pursat province.
body: On 16 November 2026 the Global Green Growth Institute reported that SchneiTec Jupiter, a Cambodian-owned special purpose company, had listed a US$99 million infrastructure project bond on the Cambodia Securities Exchange. The Institute describes it as a record green infrastructure bond for the exchange.

The bond is structured to align with the ICMA Green Bond Principles and the ASEAN Green Bond Standards, and S&P Global Ratings assigned it a “Dark Green” assessment under its Shades of Green method. The release does not state the tenor, the coupon or the arrangers.

The bond anchors a US$150 million financing package for a 350 MW solar photovoltaic plant in Krakor district, Pursat province, which is expected to power more than 200,000 Cambodian households. The plant is part of the 930 MW Chheu Tom Solar Complex. The release does not break down the rest of the package.

It moves energy, one of the seven standards: new generating capacity paid for through the nation’s own capital market rather than a sovereign loan. A sister company, SchneiTec Dynamic, listed a US$50 million bond on the exchange last year with technical assistance from the Cambodia Sustainable Bond Accelerator, which the Institute runs with funding from Luxembourg.

The model could work for Laos: a project company issues a certified green bond on its national exchange to finance a single solar plant, and a technical-assistance facility helps a young market list its first large green issues.

sources.label: Global Green Growth Institute, “Record USD99 million green infrastructure bond on Cambodia Securities Exchange anchors USD150 million solar financing package”, 16 November 2026
